newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end shade lower in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end shade lower in subdued trade.

text.p: Delhi shares closed marginally lower in cautious trade on Wednesday as prospects of an imminent hike in petroleum product prices kept major investors on the sidelines, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.07 points lower at 866.23.
"The traders were reluctant to extend their commitments before an anticipated rise in petroleum product prices," said Sharat Sharma of brokers VGS Finance.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday that the United Front coalition would decide whether to raise the prices of domestic petroleum products at its next meeting, scheduled to to be held on July 2.
Brokers said profit-taking erased early gains. "Every rise in prices attracted profit-selling which wiped out initial gains," said Dinesh Diwan of brokers Disha Investments.

Reliance Industries ended 8.80 rupees lower at 365.45 on profit-taking by speculators and financial institutions. Nearly 6.6 million shares of Reliance were traded on Wednesday, one day ahead of a company meeting to discuss a bonus share issue.
Hindustan Lever bucked the trend and surged 56.00 rupees to 1,351.00.
Hero Honda closed 4.10 rupees higher at 500.00
